Stay safe and don't keep all your money in one place.

Before you read this on how I recommend hedging your portfolio in the current environment, first read my previous tweet below it: “What Are You Hedging Against?”

The idea is simple. If your kid rides his bike only inside the house, you probably don’t need to insure it against a total loss. That would be expensive and unnecessary. You insure against the kind of damage that is actually likely to happen.

Same with hedging. First define what you are protecting against. Then build the hedge around that risk.

If everyone is already afraid of a 10% correction and hedge funds have already deleveraged, I struggle to see where the sellers come from for a full 10% drawdown.

But let’s assume they are partially right and we get a correction.

I see four possible outcomes over the next 45 days, into the October 16 expiration:

5% chance: market goes up 5% in the next 45 days

30% chance: The market goes higher. You deleveraged, so you barely participate.

30% chance: The market stays around current levels. Some stocks do well, but because you deleveraged, you probably don’t.

30% chance: We follow the historical pattern and the market corrects, but because everyone is already positioned for it, the drawdown is more like 1% to 7%, not 10%.

5% chance: The market actually falls 10% or more.

Taking that distribution into account, I like a creative hedge/trade on $QQQ into the October 16 expiration:

Buy the 715 put.
Sell 3 puts around 650, roughly 9% lower.
Sell the 750 call, roughly 5% higher.
It’s opened for a $19 credit.

The trade does especially well if the market falls somewhere between roughly 5% and 11%.

The idea is simple: stay exposed to some upside while protecting yourself against the kind of downside I think is actually more likely over the next 45 days.

I’ve spent 21 years writing about why the economy stopped working for ordinary people.

It’s not that they didn’t work hard enough, or save enough, or follow the rules. The system was rigged against them by debt and demographics, decades before most of them were even born. 

After years of chipping away at why the whole machine behaved the way it did, it all collapsed into one thing. I called it the Everything Code, because it literally explains everything… why house prices and wages stopped making any sense, why asset prices keep climbing while you keep getting poorer, why your money buys less of your future every year, why politics is so fractured and none of the old rules work anymore…

But that’s only the diagnosis. The real story is what comes next. We’re standing at the dawn of the Exponential Age, and it’ll either crush people or set them free, depending on whether they can see it coming.

Now, for the first time, all of this thinking is in one place. My first book The Everything Code is out Nov 3rd.

Preorders are open now, I’ll drop the link below for anyone interested.

Earth is just one of about 100 billion planets in our galaxy, which is just one of about two trillion galaxies in the universe. And our lifetimes are only about 1/3,000 of humanity's existence, which itself is only 1/20,000 of the Earth's existence. 

In other words, we are unbelievably tiny and short-lived and no matter what we accomplish, our impact will be insignificant. 

At the same time, we instinctually want to matter and to evolve, and we can matter a tiny bit--and it's all those tiny bits that add up to drive the evolution of the universe. #principleoftheday

Eric Weinstein's Theory on Aliens: Nukes May Have Alerted Something Else to Our Existence

@friedberg:

“What do you think, today, UAPs are?”

@ericweinstein:

“The scenario to worry about is North Sentinel Island.

Everybody who lives in North Sentinel Island is considered a citizen of India, and they don't know the word Indian.

They're an uncontacted people who don't know that they're part of something larger that watches them, that does not allow people to land.

But if they started sending out radio signals, and then they started letting off nukes on that tiny little island, India would not have this paternalistic attitude towards its primitive tribe.

So my concern is that when we let off a nuke in 1945, or when Italy became very good at quantum theory, somehow UAPs are very tied to nukes.

And I believe that a nuke is the sign that you become advanced enough that the next thing you figure out how to do is to leave and traverse through propulsion.

We alerted whatever India is in this analogy, and I believe that there are other life forms in the universe and that they can come and they can visit, and I don't think that that's preposterous.

I think that we are an uncontacted people.”
